A few points of criticism:

  • The user interface looks more like a Windows 8 desktop app than a website.

    Maybe this was your intention, but, judging from the way you worded your post, I'm guessing not.

    The user interface looks like a full screen desktop app for Windows 8, which I'm not a fan of. Websites tend to stay away from this structure style because of the simplification of features to favor appearance over usability. One would argue that simplification is good for the average user, but I'd counter argue that a website like WhoaVerse needs to have a straightforward interface with a good amount of features at close disposal to avoid confusing users.

  • The fonts and alignment are either too big or take up too much space.

    This is another issue I see right away with your mock-up. The entire structure seems inconsiderate of those who browse on smaller screen sizes or in windowed mode. These types of structures work as full-screen desktop applications on modern, larger monitors, but fail in usability when it comes to websites. Websites are browsed on a vast variety of platforms, screen sizes, ages, etc.

  • There is no sidebar for subverse descriptions or similar pieces of information.

    The sidebar information has been abandoned in this design. I assume you forgot about it or something because it can surely fit on the other side of the post list. This type of information is valuable to even familiars to provide the rules, descriptions, useful links, etc. and should be one of the first things I can see.

  • Information on the post has been omitted and shouldn't have been.

    The only information I can get out of a post from the front page is the title, how many comments there are, and which subverse the link was posted in. Not even the score has been included here, which is bad. As much information as possible should be visible on the front page without being too crowded in order to make usability smoother with less clicks.

As a desktop app, I think it lacks a lot and would frustrate many users. As a website, the interface is way to simplistic with too much whitespace and not enough options in front of users to remove unnecessary clicks.

I like the style you went with, however. Even though I abhor Windows 8 interfaces, it would be a great desktop applications if you would insert a lot more information in the areas I discussed. However, as a website design, I think it wouldn't work well at all.

I appreciate the opportunity to comment on your ideas and hope that you find my points useful.
